narrativeReportMd:
# ConceptMap R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
R6 keeps the same `ConceptMap` resource identity, but the local content model has several hard instance-breaking changes. Existing R4 instances commonly need a structural transform before R6 validation: scope fields were renamed, target equivalence was replaced by a new relationship element and code system, conditional mappings were remodeled, code-system version fields were removed, and unmapped/default behavior gained new element names and invariants.

## Scope
The comparison used the supplied R4 and R6 ConceptMap StructureDefinitions and supporting local CodeSystems for ConceptMap-specific required bindings. Inherited base-resource changes are excluded from findings.

## Main migration themes
The main theme is that R6 makes ConceptMap more explicit and operational: source and target scopes are named as scopes, code systems are canonical references, relationship direction is read from source to target, mappings can target value sets, conditional attributes and mapping properties are declared, and unmapped behavior carries explicit relationships. These improvements are not wire-compatible with R4 JSON names or code values.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are `ConceptMap:TERMINOLOGY_BINDING:target.relationship:8e57d4`, because every target mapping must migrate from R4 `equivalence` to R6 `relationship`, and `ConceptMap:SLICING_AND_CONTENT_MODEL:dependsOn:6d0ef1`, because conditional mappings changed shape and type. `ConceptMap:VALUE_CONSTRAINT:unmapped:5bb75b` is also high impact for servers implementing default translate behavior.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for mapping old equivalence codes such as `equal`, `subsumes`, `specializes`, `inexact`, and `unmatched`, and for converting conditional mapping dependencies where R4 used a free URI and string value.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several changes could have been less disruptive if R6 had retained deprecated aliases or accepted old codes for one release, but most appear aimed at clarifying semantics that were ambiguous in R4.

## Follow-up analysis
A separate terminology review should confirm any official old-code to new-code migration table. Base `Resource` and `Element` reports should own inherited language and generic constraint changes.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: ConceptMap has high-impact local breaking changes. The top migration concerns are renamed scope fields, replacement of `target.equivalence` with `target.relationship`, the remodeled `dependsOn`/property model, and stricter `unmapped` invariants. The main uncertainty is whether HL7 publishes an official lossless mapping for every old equivalence code.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is primarily a structural and terminology transform rather than an artifact-identity problem. R4 JSON element names such as `sourceCanonical`, `targetUri`, `equivalence`, `sourceVersion`, `targetVersion`, `dependsOn.property`, and `unmapped.url` are not R6 element names. R6 also introduces new validation rules that require explicit code-or-valueSet choices and explicit relationship semantics for default mappings.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural and validation findings because both primary StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared. Confidence is medium for semantic equivalence of individual code migrations because the local inputs did not include an official cross-version ConceptMap or narrative ballot rationale for the terminology redesign.

findings.title: Top-level source[x] and target[x] were renamed to sourceScope[x] and targetScope[x]

oldState.summary: R4 used `source[x]` and `target[x]` choice elements for the source and target value-set context.

semanticText.definition: Identifier for the source value set that contains the concepts that are being mapped and provides context for the mappings.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4 the JSON choice property names are `sourceUri`, `sourceCanonical`, `targetUri`, and `targetCanonical`.

newState.summary: R6 uses `sourceScope[x]` and `targetScope[x]` with the same cardinality and value-set choice types.

semanticText.definition: Identifier for the source value set that contains the concepts that are being mapped and provides context for the mappings. Limits the scope of the map to source codes that are members of this value set.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6 the equivalent JSON choice property names are `sourceScopeUri`, `sourceScopeCanonical`, `targetScopeUri`, and `targetScopeCanonical`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new elements have the same parent, same cardinality, same choice types, same value-set target profile, same summary flag, and closely matching definitions. The R6 name clarifies that these value sets define mapping scope rather than the code system itself.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a wire-format break. An R4 instance containing `sourceCanonical` or `targetUri` uses elements that do not exist in R6, so strict R6 validation rejects them. Generated model classes and FHIRPath expressions that reference `source` or `target` for value-set scope must be renamed.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is primarily data rejection or incorrect map scoping, not direct clinical harm, but incorrect scoping can affect terminology translation outcomes.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify that these elements are value-set scopes rather than the source and target code systems used by groups.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 `source[x]` and `target[x]` element names in base R6 and clarify in definitions that they are value-set scopes.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The clarity goal is reasonable: top-level `source[x]` and `target[x]` are value-set scopes, not the group code systems. But the R6 elements kept the same cardinality and types, so the main break is a rename. Because the same goal could mostly be met by retaining the R4 names with clearer short/definition text and examples, the hard instance break looks probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design is not a conversion tool or extension; it is to keep `ConceptMap.source[x]` and `ConceptMap.target[x]` as the canonical base elements and update their definitions to say source scope and target scope. Adding parallel `sourceScope[x]` aliases would also preserve old instances, but it would create two same-resource ways to say the same thing and deprecated spellings might linger indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This leaves less precise names and some confusion with group source/target, but avoids a wire-format break without duplicating representations.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `ConceptMap.source[x]` as 0..1 uri or canonical(ValueSet), summary true.
R6 defines `ConceptMap.sourceScope[x]` as 0..1 uri or canonical(ValueSet), summary true.
R4 defines `ConceptMap.target[x]` for target value-set context.
R6 defines `ConceptMap.targetScope[x]` for target value-set scope.

examples.examplesMd: The example isolates the renamed fields; a complete ConceptMap would also include mapping groups.

findings.narrativeMd: `ConceptMap.source[x]` and `ConceptMap.target[x]` did not disappear semantically, but their element identities changed. This is still a hard instance break because FHIR JSON uses the element name in the serialized property. A data transform can usually rename the fields without loss.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances with `sourceUri`, `sourceCanonical`, `targetUri`, or `targetCanonical` fail R6 validation because those properties are not R6 children. R6 instances with `sourceScope*` or `targetScope*` are not directly valid R4. The transform is straightforward if the old and new fields are not both present.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `sourceUri` to `sourceScopeUri`, `sourceCanonical` to `sourceScopeCanonical`, `targetUri` to `targetScopeUri`, and `targetCanonical` to `targetScopeCanonical`. Update generated accessors, FHIRPath, search/extraction logic, and tests that assumed top-level `source` or `target` names.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The rename was probably intended to resolve ambiguity with `group.source` and `group.target`. A backward-compatible alternative would have been to accept old aliases as deprecated elements or extensions during a transition period, but that would keep ambiguous terminology in the base model.

findings.title: Group code-system references changed from uri plus separate version fields to canonical CodeSystem references

oldState.summary: R4 `group.source` and `group.target` were plain `uri`; `group.sourceVersion` and `group.targetVersion` held separate code-system version strings.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented the code-system identity and version in separate sibling elements.

newState.summary: R6 `group.source` and `group.target` are `canonical(CodeSystem)` and the separate version elements are absent.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 expects code-system references to be canonical references. Version information, when needed, must be represented through canonical-reference conventions or external policy rather than the removed sibling fields.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The group source and target element names remain stable, but their type domains changed. The removed version elements were direct children of the same group and were not replaced by separate R6 children.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance that uses `sourceVersion` or `targetVersion` contains elements that R6 does not define. Even when those fields are absent, generated code and validators see `source` and `target` as canonical CodeSystem references in R6 rather than generic URIs.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Losing or misplacing code-system version information can change terminology translation results for systems where code meanings or membership changed by version.

justification.inferredGoal: Align group code-system references with canonical resource reference semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `sourceVersion` and `targetVersion` alongside canonical `group.source` and `group.target`, with explicit precedence rules for versioned canonicals.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Aligning group source and target with canonical CodeSystem references is a reasonable R6 goal. A less-breaking base design could preserve the removed version siblings, but version information can change terminology translation results; allowing both canonical `|version` syntax and separate version fields creates validation ambiguity and interoperability risk. Those material tradeoffs make the simplifying break probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative would keep `ConceptMap.group.sourceVersion` and `ConceptMap.group.targetVersion` as deprecated optional elements while encouraging canonical CodeSystem references in `group.source` and `group.target`. That would preserve R4 instances with explicit version strings, but R6 would need rules for whether `group.source` may include a version suffix, which value wins on conflict, and how systems round-trip or compare the two representations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves old version data but creates duplicate version locations and conflict-handling requirements.

evidence.detail: R4 `group.source` type is `uri`.
R6 `group.source` type is `canonical` targeting CodeSystem.
R4 has `sourceVersion` 0..1 string.
No R6 `ConceptMap.group.sourceVersion` or `ConceptMap.group.targetVersion` element is present.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows one possible canonical-version representation. Implementers should verify the allowed canonical version syntax and local convention before applying it broadly.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 separated code-system identity from code-system version at the group level. R6 removes the version siblings and changes the remaining identity fields to canonical CodeSystem references. The structural break is clear for any stored R4 data that populated the version fields.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `group.sourceVersion` or `group.targetVersion` are old-valid/new-invalid because those elements are absent in R6. R6 canonical references may be serializable as strings in R4, but R4 consumers will not necessarily understand versioned canonical syntax unless a transform splits the canonical into URI plus version.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory ConceptMaps that use group version fields. Decide whether to encode versions into canonical references, preserve them in extensions, or maintain version policy outside the resource. Test maps where source and target code-system versions affect equivalence decisions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change improves alignment with canonical references, but separate version fields could have remained optional and deprecated without invalidating old data. The less-breaking alternative would require extra rules for conflicts between a versioned canonical and the old version fields.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is recommended for code systems with non-permanent concepts or where old version strings are not valid canonical version suffixes.

findings.title: target.equivalence was replaced by target.relationship with a different required code system and direction

oldState.summary: R4 required modifier element `equivalence` 1..1, bound required to `concept-map-equivalence` with ten codes.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The old ValueSet was not expanded by a terminology server; codes were read from the local CodeSystem recursively.

flags.isModifierReason: Some values mean that there is no mapping from the source to the target.

semanticText.definition: The equivalence is read from target to source.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used `equivalence` values such as `equal`, `wider`, `subsumes`, `narrower`, `specializes`, `inexact`, `unmatched`, and `disjoint`.

newState.summary: R6 requires modifier element `relationship` 1..1, bound required to `concept-map-relationship` with five codes.

changedCodes.oldMeaning: R4 `equivalent` meant the definitions mean the same thing including structural implications.
changedCodes.newMeaning: R6 `equivalent` means the definitions mean the same thing.
changedCodes.changeSummary: The code string is retained but in a different code system and with shorter definition text.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The new relationship is read from source to target, reversing the orientation stated on the old equivalence element.

flags.isModifierReason: The `not-related-to` relationship means there is no mapping.

semanticText.definition: The relationship is read from source to target.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both elements are required modifier codes under `ConceptMap.group.element.target` and both express the semantic relationship between source and target concepts.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Every R4 target mapping has a required `equivalence` element that is absent in R6. R6 instead requires `relationship`. Required terminology binding also changed, so old codes such as `relatedto`, `wider`, `narrower`, `inexact`, `unmatched`, and `disjoint` are not valid R6 relationship codes. Because the stated reading direction changed, simple string replacement can invert meaning if done carelessly.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect equivalence/relationship migration can cause terminology translation to return mappings with the wrong semantic strength or direction.

justification.inferredGoal: Simplify and clarify ConceptMap relationship semantics by using source-to-target relationship names.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `relationship` for new source-to-target semantics while retaining legacy `equivalence` as a deprecated mutually exclusive alternative during transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of source-to-target relationship names is reasonable and addresses a real R4 ambiguity. A base R6 design could have accepted legacy `equivalence`, but old ten-code equivalence semantics do not map cleanly to the R6 five-code relationship system, and the reading direction changes. Keeping both modifier representations would carry a meaningful safety and interoperability burden, so the breaking redesign is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would model the target relationship as accepting either the old `equivalence` element or the new `relationship` element, with an invariant that only one appears. This is only a partial alternative: implementations would still need to understand old target-to-source semantics, distinguish close-but-not-identical codes such as `equal` and `equivalent`, and handle legacy codes such as `inexact` and `unmatched`. A cross-version ConceptMap would help migration, but by itself it is conversion guidance rather than a backward-compatible base R6 design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves old target entries but leaves two modifier elements, two code systems, and opposite reading directions in the base resource.

evidence.detail: R4 `equivalence` is 1..1 code, isModifier true, required binding to `concept-map-equivalence|4.0.1`.
evidence.quote: The equivalence is read from target to source.

evidence.detail: R6 `relationship` is 1..1 code, isModifier true, required binding to `concept-map-relationship|6.0.0-ballot4`.
evidence.quote: The relationship is read from source to target.

evidence.detail: Local code systems show R4 has ten equivalence codes while R6 has five relationship codes.

examples.examplesMd: The example maps R4 `wider` to the likely R6 source-to-target direction. Old `equal` versus `equivalent`, `subsumes` versus `wider`, and `unmatched` versus `disjoint` may require policy decisions.

findings.narrativeMd: The central target relationship element was renamed and re-termed. This is a hard validation break and a semantic migration hazard: the R4 element says to read the relationship from target to source, while R6 names the relationship from source to target. Code-value migration should be handled as terminology mapping, not as a blind rename.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 target with `equivalence` is invalid in R6 because R6 requires `relationship` and does not define `equivalence`. R6 `relationship` values are not directly valid R4 equivalence values. The change affects strict validators, generated enums, switch statements, mapping engines, and any code that interprets modifier values.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Build an explicit migration table and review it with terminology owners. Likely mappings include `relatedto` to `related-to`, `equivalent` or `equal` to `equivalent` with possible loss of distinction, `wider` or `subsumes` to `source-is-narrower-than-target`, `narrower` or `specializes` to `source-is-broader-than-target`, and `disjoint` to `not-related-to`. Treat `inexact` and `unmatched` as needing manual review or map-specific policy.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 design is easier to read and likely avoids R4 orientation confusion. A backward-compatible alternative would have accepted old `equivalence` codes as deprecated aliases and emitted warnings, but that would have preserved a confusing target-to-source interpretation and two overlapping code systems.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The suggested code mappings are inferred from local definitions, not from an official cross-version ConceptMap.

findings.title: Conditional mapping dependencies were remodeled around additionalAttribute and typed value[x]/valueSet

oldState.summary: R4 dependency rows used required `property` uri and required `value` string, with optional `system` canonical(CodeSystem) and `display` string.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 put the dependency property identity and string value directly on each `dependsOn` entry.

newState.summary: R6 dependency rows use required `attribute` code referencing `ConceptMap.additionalAttribute`, plus either typed `value[x]` or `valueSet`.

constraints.human: One of value[x] or valueSet must exist, but not both.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 separates attribute definition from dependency usage and supports typed dependency values or value-set membership.

facts.newValue: cmd-6 requires exactly one of value[x] or valueSet

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The parent `dependsOn` element remains in place and its definition still says the mapping applies only if another data attribute has a specified value. The child shape, typing, and declaration model changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances using conditional mappings have child elements that do not exist in R6. R6 requires a declared additional attribute and typed value choice or value set. R6 conditions using boolean, Quantity, Coding, or valueSet cannot be represented losslessly in the R4 string-only dependency shape.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect dependency migration can make a mapping apply in contexts where it should not, or fail to apply where it should.

justification.inferredGoal: Make mapping dependencies typed, declared, and reusable by translate operations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `additionalAttribute` and typed `value[x]`/`valueSet` while retaining R4 `dependsOn.property`, `system`, `value`, and `display` as deprecated legacy children.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 model is materially clearer: dependencies are declared once, referenced by code, and can carry typed values or value-set membership. Retaining the R4 tuple would reduce migration pain, but the R4 free-string `value` and URI `property` do not provide the same validation or reusable attribute semantics. Because supporting both shapes would add ambiguity and implementation burden for translate behavior, the break is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative would allow the old `property`/`system`/`value`/`display` children as deprecated legacy fields while adding the R6 declaration and typed-value model. That would preserve R4 instances, but R6 would need conflict rules when both legacy and typed fields appear, guidance for deriving `additionalAttribute` declarations from arbitrary URIs, and handling for old string values that are really codes, paths, text, or value-set identifiers.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This keeps old conditional maps valid but creates two condition models and weakens the typed declaration guarantees.

evidence.detail: R4 `dependsOn.property` is 1..1 uri.
R4 `dependsOn.value` is 1..1 string.
R6 `dependsOn.attribute` is 1..1 code referencing `ConceptMap.additionalAttribute`.
R6 adds error invariant cmd-6: one of value[x] or valueSet must exist, but not both.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments show the affected backbone entry, not a complete resource. R6 typed values may need policy to choose `valueCode`, `valueCoding`, `valueString`, `valueBoolean`, `valueQuantity`, or `valueSet`.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 turns R4's ad hoc dependency tuple into a declared and typed attribute model. This affects both the wire shape and business logic because dependency matching is what determines whether a target mapping applies in a specific context.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 dependency children `property`, `system`, `value`, and `display` are old-valid/new-invalid. R6 dependency entries are invalid unless exactly one of `value[x]` or `valueSet` is present. R6 typed values and value-set dependencies are not losslessly representable in R4's required string `value` field.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For each distinct R4 dependency property, create a `ConceptMap.additionalAttribute` with a stable code, URI, description, and type. Then replace `dependsOn.property` with `dependsOn.attribute` and map the old string value into the appropriate R6 `value[x]` or `valueSet`. Add tests for each conditional branch of a map.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The redesign is probably justified by stronger typing and reusability, but the old tuple shape could have been retained as deprecated fields. That alternative would have preserved old instances while weakening R6's ability to validate dependency values consistently.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Reviewers should check maps where the R4 `value` string contained a path, text expression, implicit value-set identifier, or code display rather than a clean code.

findings.title: R6 requires explicit code-or-valueSet choices and adds noMap/valueSet mapping forms

affectedLocation.newPath: ConceptMap.group.element.code or valueSet / ConceptMap.group.element.target.code or valueSet / ConceptMap.group.element.noMap

oldState.summary: R4 had optional source `code` and optional target `code`; it did not have source or target `valueSet` children or `noMap`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 permitted mapping entries where a source or target code was omitted, with semantics often inferred from group scope or equivalence values such as `unmatched`.

newState.summary: R6 adds source and target `valueSet` choices, `group.element.noMap`, and invariants requiring exactly one of code or valueSet for source and target mapping entries.

constraints.human: If noMap is present and has a value of true, target SHALL NOT be present
Either code or valueSet SHALL be present but not both.
Either code or valueSet SHALL be present but not both.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can express a mapping rule for a set of source concepts, a target value set, or an explicit no-map assertion, but it also rejects entries that do not identify source and target content precisely.

facts.newValue: cmd-5 requires either source code or source valueSet but not both
cmd-7 requires either target code or target valueSet but not both

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 additions are direct children of the same mapping-entry and target-entry backbones and constrain elements that existed in R4.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 data that omitted source or target codes can become invalid under R6 error invariants unless it is converted to the new `valueSet` or `noMap` forms. Conversely, R6 value-set-to-value-set rules and `noMap` assertions have no native R4 representation.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: A wrong conversion between `unmatched`, `noMap`, empty target, and value-set mappings can change translate behavior for unmapped concepts.

justification.inferredGoal: Support set-based mapping rules and make no-map assertions explicit while preventing ambiguous source and target entries.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `valueSet` and `noMap` but make the code-or-valueSet rules warnings, or permit constrained legacy entries that omit both fields.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Supporting source and target value sets and an explicit `noMap` flag is a reasonable model improvement. The breaking part is the new error-level requirement that mapping entries identify exactly one code or value set. A less-breaking design could accept older omitted-code patterns, but that would undercut the R6 guarantee that each rule precisely identifies what it maps, and ambiguity around empty targets versus no-map assertions can affect translation behavior.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The partial base alternative would add the new R6 fields while relaxing `cmd-5` and `cmd-7` to warnings or carving out legacy cases where neither `code` nor `valueSet` is present. This is not merely migration tooling; it would preserve old instances in the base validator. The tradeoff is that R6 consumers would still have to interpret underspecified source or target entries and distinguish incomplete data from deliberate no-map behavior.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves permissive R4 maps but keeps ambiguous mapping and no-map semantics in the base resource.

evidence.detail: R4 source `code` is 0..1 and no sibling `valueSet` is present.
R6 adds invariant cmd-5 requiring either source code or source valueSet but not both.
R6 adds invariant cmd-7 requiring either target code or target valueSet but not both.
R6 adds `noMap` 0..1 boolean with a constraint that no target is present when noMap is true.

examples.examplesMd: The old fragment shows an omitted source and target code pattern that R4 cardinalities allowed. The R6 fragment shows set-based mapping and noMap semantics that R4 cannot represent natively.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 makes mapping entry identity explicit: a source entry identifies either one code or one value set, and a target entry identifies either one code or one value set. It also introduces `noMap` as a direct way to say that no target exists. These are useful model improvements but create validation breaks for permissive R4 maps and round-trip loss for R6 set-based maps.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 map entry with neither `code` nor a migratable value set becomes invalid under R6 cmd-5. A target entry with neither `code` nor `valueSet` becomes invalid under cmd-7. If `noMap=true`, R6 also requires the target list to be empty. R6 `valueSet` and `noMap` content is not cleanly representable in R4 except through extensions or lossy conventions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: During R4-to-R6 migration, determine whether omitted codes actually mean a source/target value set, an explicit no-map assertion, or incomplete data. Use `group.element.valueSet`, `target.valueSet`, or `group.element.noMap` as appropriate. Add validation tests for code-only, valueSet-only, both-present, and neither-present cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The new invariants are likely justified because they prevent ambiguous mappings. Backward compatibility could have been improved by allowing old omitted-code patterns with warnings, but that would weaken the R6 guarantee that each mapping rule identifies what it maps.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Pay special attention to R4 `equivalence=unmatched` entries; some should become R6 `noMap=true`, while others may be better represented as `relationship=not-related-to` with an explicit target.

findings.title: group.unmapped changed mode code, renamed url to otherMap, and added stricter relationship/default constraints

affectedLocation.newPath: ConceptMap.group.unmapped.mode / code / display / valueSet / relationship / otherMap / comment

oldState.summary: R4 unmapped mode codes were `provided`, `fixed`, and `other-map`; `url` held the fallback ConceptMap when mode was `other-map`.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R4 code system has `provided`, `fixed`, and `other-map`.

constraints.human: If the mode is fixed, a code must be provided
If the mode is other-map, a url must be provided

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 default behavior did not have an explicit relationship field for fixed or provided mappings.

newState.summary: R6 mode codes are `use-source-code`, `fixed`, and `other-map`; `otherMap` replaces `url`; `relationship` is required except for `other-map`; `valueSet` can supply fixed targets.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R6 code system replaces R4 `provided` with `use-source-code`.

constraints.human: If the mode is fixed, either a code or valueSet must be provided, but not both.
constraints.expression: (mode = 'fixed') implies ((code.exists() and valueSet.empty()) or (code.empty() and valueSet.exists()))

constraints.human: If the mode is other-map, a url for the other map must be provided
If the mode is not fixed, code, display and valueSet are not allowed
If the mode is not other-map, relationship must be provided
If the mode is not other-map, otherMap is not allowed

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes default mapping semantics explicit by requiring a default relationship for use-source-code or fixed modes.

facts.newValue: cmd-9 requires relationship when mode is not other-map

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `unmapped` remains the same backbone for default behavior when no mapping target is found. The child model and required mode semantics changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `mode=provided` is not an R6 code, R4 `url` is not an R6 element, and R4 fixed/provided defaults lack the R6 `relationship` required by cmd-9. These changes affect validation and terminology translate behavior for any map that defines default handling.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Default handling controls what translation returns when no explicit target is found; an incorrect migration can silently produce different target codes.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify default unmapped behavior and align it with the new relationship code system.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `provided` and `url` as deprecated aliases and allow legacy fixed/provided defaults without `relationship`, or define an explicit legacy default.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying unmapped behavior and requiring an explicit default relationship for fixed or source-code defaults is a reasonable R6 goal. A less-breaking base design could preserve the old mode code and old fallback-map element name, but preserving all R4 instances also means accepting R4 defaults that lack the new `relationship`. That missing modifier value is semantically important, so the alternative is only partial and carries operational risk.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative would accept `mode=provided` as a deprecated alias for `use-source-code` and `unmapped.url` as a deprecated alias for `otherMap`. For `other-map`, that mostly preserves old content. For `fixed` and `provided`, however, preserving old instances requires either making `relationship` optional for legacy content or assigning a default relationship; both choices can misstate the intended translation relationship and leave validators with special-case legacy rules.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Aliases preserve some old data, but accepting or guessing missing relationships weakens default mapping semantics and can change translate results.

evidence.detail: R4 mode required binding lists `provided | fixed | other-map`.
R6 mode required binding lists `use-source-code | fixed | other-map`.
R4 `url` is 0..1 canonical(ConceptMap).
R6 `otherMap` is 0..1 canonical(ConceptMap).
R6 adds cmd-8, cmd-9, and cmd-10 constraints that restrict code/display/valueSet, require relationship for non-other-map modes, and forbid otherMap outside other-map mode.

examples.examplesMd: R4 `provided` usually maps to R6 `use-source-code`, but the required R6 `relationship` requires a semantic decision.

findings.narrativeMd: The `unmapped` backbone changed from a relatively compact default-action model to a stricter model that names the source-code behavior, renames the fallback map reference, supports fixed value sets, and requires an explicit relationship for defaults. This is both a validation break and a runtime behavior risk.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `mode=provided` fails R6 required binding validation. R4 `unmapped.url` is invalid because R6 uses `otherMap`. R4 fixed or provided defaults without `relationship` fail R6 cmd-9. R6 fixed value-set defaults and comments have no native R4 fields.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `provided` to `use-source-code`, rename `url` to `otherMap`, and add an explicit `relationship` for `use-source-code` and `fixed` modes. For `fixed`, choose either `code` or `valueSet`, not both. Test translate behavior for explicit matches, no explicit match with default, and other-map fallback.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The stricter R6 model is likely justified because default translation output should state its relationship. A backward-compatible transition could have accepted old names and old mode codes as aliases, but that would undermine the clean R6 model.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The correct default `relationship` for `use-source-code` may vary by map. Do not assume `equivalent` without reviewing the map purpose.

findings.title: R6 adds declared mapping properties and typed target.property values that R4 cannot round-trip

oldState.summary: R4 had no native `ConceptMap.property`, `target.property`, or `additionalAttribute` declaration blocks.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could only carry comparable information through extensions or overloaded comments/dependencies.

newState.summary: R6 adds `ConceptMap.property` definitions, `target.property` values with typed `value[x]`, and `additionalAttribute` declarations used by dependencies and products.

constraints.human: If the property type is code, a system SHALL be specified

newState.narrativeMd: R6 provides first-class support for metadata on individual source-to-target mapping relationships.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: These are new R6 ConceptMap-local backbones with no R4 element ids. They are related to the dependency remodel but also support new target mapping properties.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances are not invalid merely because R6 adds optional elements, so this is not an old-valid/new-invalid break for ordinary core R4 content. It is a high R6-to-R4 risk because native R6 mapping properties and typed values have no R4 home, and R4 extension-based conventions need deliberate mapping into the new declaration structures.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Mapping properties can influence ranking, equivalence policy, provenance, or translate output; losing them can change operational results.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent per-mapping properties and translate-operation attributes explicitly instead of relying on extensions or comments.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because optional R6 `property`, `target.property`, and `additionalAttribute` content does not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: First-class typed mapping properties and declared additional attributes are reasonable R6 additions. This finding is not an old-valid/new-invalid base-design break: ordinary R4 ConceptMap instances remain valid with respect to these optional additions. The reported risk is R6-to-R4 round-trip loss, so backward-compatible alternative availability for the R4-to-R6 base design is not applicable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed to preserve R4 instances for this finding. Omitting the new elements would fail the R6 goal of native typed mapping metadata, while R4 extensions or cross-version transforms can reduce down-conversion loss but are mitigations outside the base R6 content model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 export may need extensions or data loss; that is a conversion mitigation, not a less-breaking base R6 alternative.

evidence.detail: R6 adds `ConceptMap.property` 0..* summary backbone for additional mapping properties.
R6 target property values are 1..1 choices over Coding, string, integer, boolean, dateTime, decimal, and code.
R6 adds `ConceptMap.additionalAttribute` 0..* summary backbone for attributes used as data source or target.
No corresponding R4 `ConceptMap.property`, `target.property`, or `additionalAttribute` element is present.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 migration example is only a placeholder extension strategy; no official R4 extension was found in the supplied inputs.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds first-class property declarations and per-target typed property values. This expands ConceptMap's ability to support operational mapping metadata, but it creates a one-way feature for R6 content unless R4 systems agree on extensions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Simple R4 instances do not fail R6 validation because these elements are optional. The break appears in conversion and code generation: R6 instances using these fields cannot be represented as core R4 ConceptMap content, and R4 extension-based conventions need deliberate mapping into R6 declarations and typed values.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When migrating to R6, identify any R4 extensions or comments that represent mapping rank, status, provenance, or operational attributes and convert them to `ConceptMap.property` plus `target.property` where appropriate. For R6-to-R4 export, preserve native R6 properties in extensions and document the loss of native R4 semantics.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The new model is additive for R6 but not backward-compatible for round-trip with R4. Standard cross-version extensions would be the least disruptive compatibility mechanism.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Because this finding is mainly R6-to-R4 and extension-convention risk, projects with simple R4 maps and no per-target properties may not be affected.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, abstract flag, derivation, and base definition remain ConceptMap/resource/specialization of DomainResource. R6 is present at the expected StructureDefinition path.

No local existing ConceptMap element was found with a direct min-cardinality increase or max-cardinality decrease. Material cardinality-like breaks are instead caused by removed elements and new R6 invariants covered in findings. `ConceptMap.identifier` widened from 0..1 to 0..*.

The material local type-domain change found was `group.source`/`group.target` from uri to canonical(CodeSystem), covered as a finding. Other same-id local elements retained their main datatypes, aside from new R6 elements.

Required ConceptMap-specific binding changes for target relationship and unmapped mode are findings. `status` remains required with the same visible codes `draft | active | retired | unknown`; `jurisdiction` remains extensible though its value set URL moved to terminology.hl7.org.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value change was identified on ConceptMap elements.

The required target relationship remains modifier-like in R6, replacing the R4 modifier `equivalence`. New `group.unmapped.relationship` is also a modifier element and is covered under unmapped behavior. No unrelated modifier-flag change was identified.

Existing summary behavior is materially preserved for the renamed source/target scope elements. New R6 summary elements such as `property`, `additionalAttribute`, and metadata fields may affect `_summary` payload shape but are additive.
No local slicing discriminator or slice-rule change was identified for ConceptMap in the compared StructureDefinitions.

Serialization breaks are concentrated in renamed or removed JSON properties and choice names covered by findings. No separate representation-format change beyond those element-model changes was identified.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: ConceptMap.identifier widened from 0..1 to 0..*
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Increasing maximum cardinality does not invalidate R4 instances in R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 instances with multiple identifiers cannot round-trip into core R4 without dropping identifiers or using extensions.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds canonical-resource metadata fields
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Fields such as `versionAlgorithm[x]`, `copyrightLabel`, `approvalDate`, `lastReviewDate`, `effectivePeriod`, `topic`, `author`, `editor`, `reviewer`, `endorser`, and `relatedArtifact` are optional additions.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6-to-R4 export needs extensions or data loss for these metadata fields. `relatedArtifact` also has an R6 constraint forbidding `depends-on` and `composed-of` types in ConceptMap.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: ConceptMap StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is metadata about the definition, not an instance content-model break.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The maturity/status shift may affect governance decisions that previously treated ConceptMap as draft.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Jurisdiction binding value set URL moved to terminology.hl7.org
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `jurisdiction` remains 0..* CodeableConcept with extensible binding, so ordinary R4 instances are not rejected solely by the URL change.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology tooling should use the R6 value set URL `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/jurisdiction` when validating R6 artifacts.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Comment requirement for weaker mappings changed from R4 error to R6 warning for selected relationships
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R4 `cmd-1` error requiring comments for `narrower` or `inexact` was replaced by an R6 warning for `source-is-broader-than-target` or `not-related-to` unless the resource is draft.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Although not a validation hardening, map quality rules and test suites may need to adjust expected diagnostics.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: A terminology owner should confirm the official migration from R4 equivalence codes to R6 relationship codes, especially for `equal`, `subsumes`, `specializes`, `inexact`, and `unmatched`.
Inherited base changes, including generic constraints and `Resource.language` binding behavior, are intentionally excluded from this ConceptMap-local report.
The remodel of `relationship`, `dependsOn`, `property`, and `unmapped` likely affects operation input/output semantics beyond what the StructureDefinition alone can prove.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 ConceptMap diff, ballot rationale, or migration guide was included in the local inputs. Structural differences are clear, but rationale and intended compatibility mappings are partly inferred.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use an official HL7 cross-version diff or published migration notes for ConceptMap.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Required binding code lists were read from local CodeSystem resources rather than a live terminology expansion service. This is adequate for the core ConceptMap-specific codes inspected, but it does not prove all value-set expansion behavior.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run terminology expansions for the R4 and R6 value sets and compare them with any official cross-version mapping.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The assessment is primarily StructureDefinition-driven. Narrative specification pages and OperationDefinition behavior for ConceptMap translation were not exhaustively compared.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the R4 and R6 ConceptMap narrative pages and `$translate` OperationDefinition side by side.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Expected prevalence is estimated from element purpose and typical ConceptMap usage, not from a corpus of production R4 ConceptMap instances.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Scan a representative corpus of R4 ConceptMap resources for usage of source/target scope fields, sourceVersion/targetVersion, dependsOn, unmapped, and equivalence codes.
